cover_letter.greeting: Dear Crusoe Real Estate Finance Team,
paragraphs: I'm applying for the Financial Analyst, Real Estate, Land & Leases role at Crusoe. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. What interests me is your point that land and power access are often the binding constraint on how fast infrastructure gets built. That makes site-level economics a real input into what gets built and when.

My closest experience is an MBA project: I built project- and portfolio-level financial models for a 6-project, 35.4 MW Illinois solar portfolio, evaluating capital structure, DSCR, NPV and levered IRR under post-ITC scenarios. I compared senior debt with green loan + ABS structures, and the phased green loan + ABS recommendation reduced sponsor equity by $11.1M in the model and improved levered IRR from 8.58% to 9.79%. At Lenovo I built models and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%.

That maps to the site-level models and to the work on how ownership and lease structures affect financing. The solar project was coursework, not a live transaction, and ground leases would be new to me, so I'd expect to learn a lot from the Real Estate and Project Finance teams. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
